headline: DU student blocked from using washroom and assaulted, allegations
summary: A student of the Television, Film & Photography department has accused another student of the Bijoy Ekattor Hall of assault and threats during a clash over washroom access.
details: Ahmed Shahariar, a student of the 2023-24 session of the Television, Film & Photography department, has filed a written complaint against fellow student Abdullah Al Mahfuz of the 2020-21 session (Bengali department).

The incident occurred on Sunday night after midnight, during the World Cup final. Shahariar alleges that Mahfuz blocked him from entering a washroom near the guest room of Bijoy Ekattor Hall, telling him to use another washroom which he found locked.

Shahariar claims that when he returned to question the blockage, a verbal altercation occurred. He alleges that Mahfuz threatened to take him to a guest room to 'teach him manners' and threatened to block his washroom access for the entire night.
The complainant further alleges that he was assaulted and verbally abused. He submitted a written complaint to the Provost of Bijoy Ekattor Hall, Professor S M Ali Reza, on Monday night.
Abdullah Al Mahfuz has denied the allegations. He claims that female guests who had come to watch the game were using the washroom, and he was standing outside to ensure their privacy.

Mahfuz asserts that he asked Shahariar to wait two minutes, but Shahariar objected to the female guests' presence in the guest room late at night. and then used disrespectful language toward him as a junior.

The Provost of Bijoy Ekattor Hall, Professor S M Ali Reza, stated that he initially tried to mediate a settlement between the two students, but formed a formal investigation committee after mutual accusations continued.
The investigation committee has been requested to submit its report within the next four working days.

The conflict has also seen political affiliationsy as the Bijoy Ekattor Hall branch of Chhatra Dal maintains that the𝗹𝗹𝗲𝗴𝗲𝗱 assailant is linked to Bangladesh Islami Chhatra Shibir, deuda a a claim denied by Chhatra Shibir's DU branch editor.
The complainant, Ahmed Shahariar, is identified as a member of the hall's Chhatra Dal branch.

headline: SAARC and BIMSTEC are complementary platforms, says State Minister
summary: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaid Islam emphasizes that both regional organizations can coexist and drive development for Bangladesh and the region.
details: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaid Islam stated that SAARC and BIMSTEC are complementary and can function effectively side-by-side to ensure the development of the region and its people.

Speaking at a seminar titled 'Three Decades of BIMSTEC: Advancing Regional Cooperation for Joint Prosperity' organized by the Bangladesh Institute of International and Strategic Studies (BIISS) in Dhaka.
The State Minister noted that SAARC was a vision of late President Ziaur Rahman to improve connectivity, trade, and living standards in South Asia, though the initiative has slowed down over time.
She affirmed that the BNP-led government, after being elected by the people, will take initiatives to revitalize SAARC, as outlined in their election manifesto.
Regarding BIMSTEC, she described it as a crucial multilateral platform, noting that since many of its members are not part of SAARC, the two organizations complement each other.
As Bangladesh currently holds the BIMSTEC presidency, the State Minister reaffirmed the country's commitment to making the Bay of Bengal region peaceful, resilient, and prosperous.
She emphasized the focus on economic integration, connectivity, trade, investment, the blue economy, and people-centric regional cooperation.
BIMSTEC Secretary General Indra Mani Pandey also detailed ongoing projects in women's development, climate adaptation, energy interconnection, and counter-terrorism.
caption:
Can SAARC and BIMSTEC coexist? State Minister Shama Obaid Islam says yes—and they are complementary.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaid Islam stated that SAARC and BIMSTEC are complementary and can function effectively side-by-side to ensure the development of the region and its people.

Speaking at a seminar titled 'Three Decades of BIMSTEC: Advancing Regional Cooperation for Joint Prosperity' organized by the Bangladesh Institute of International and Strategic Studies (BIISS) in Dhaka.

The State Minister noted that SAARC was a vision of late President Ziaur Rahman to improve connectivity, trade, and living standards in South Asia, though the initiative has slowed down over time.

She affirmed that the BNP-led government, after being elected by the people, will take initiatives to revitalize SAARC, as outlined in their election manifesto.

Regarding BIMSTEC, she described it as a crucial multilateral platform, noting that since many of its members are not part of SAARC, the two organizations complement each other.

As Bangladesh currently holds the BIMSTEC presidency, the State Minister reaffirmed the country's commitment to making the Bay of Bengal region peaceful, resilient, and prosperous.

She emphasized the focus on economic integration, connectivity, trade, investment, the blue economy, and people-centric regional cooperation.

BIMSTEC Secretary General Indra Mani Pandey also detailed ongoing projects in women's development, climate adaptation, energy interconnection, and counter-terrorism.
